blocks.content: Explore an unstacked panel and a stacked one to see what a stacked boundary means.
Find **Lines** in the **Styles** row. It's unstacked, which is stacking **Off**.
Hover at one time and read its value. Each line is measured from zero.
Focus on **Stacked lines**, further down. Its stacking is **Normal**.
Hover at one time. Each series sits on top of the one below, so the top boundary is their total, not the top series' own value. Read individual values from the tooltip.
The third mode, **100%**, isn't shown here. It rescales every point in time to 100 percent, so you see each series' share of the total and lose the total itself.
Stacking can mislead and hide data. The Grafana docs recommend turning it off in most cases.
You've compared Off and Normal stacking. Check the mode before you read a boundary as a value.
